text: A scruffy stray dog trots up and sits at your feet. It watches you with absolute faith.

choices.label: Feed it a bit (@3)
choices.text: It wolfs the food and leans against your leg.

choices.label: Shoo it away
choices.text: It trots off, looking back once.

text: Your phone buzzes. {friend}, an old friend from the city: "Can you spot me @20? Rent's killing me."

choices.label: Send @20
choices.text: She sends back a string of hearts.

choices.label: Leave it on read
choices.text: You put the phone away. It stays heavy in your pocket.

text: A brown leather wallet lies on the pavement, a driver's license peeking out.

choices.label: Return it
choices.text: The owner is stunned, then grateful. He hands you a ten.

choices.label: Keep the cash
choices.text: You pocket the bills and drop the wallet in a bin.

text: {cook} slides a plate across the counter. "On the house. You look like you need it."

choices.label: Accept graciously
choices.text: You eat every bite.

text: Two guys block the alley mouth. One cracks his knuckles. "Wrong place, wrong time."

win.text: You land a few good ones and they back off.

lose.text: They beat you down and take your cash.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.text: You back off and cut across the street, heart hammering.

text: The power cuts out with a pop. Total darkness.

choices.label: Wait it out
choices.text: You sit by the window and listen to the town breathe.

text: A patrol car slows beside you. The officer gets out. "Got a minute? We've had some reports."

win.text: Smiles, shrugs, a plausible story. He lets you go.

lose.text: He isn't buying it. Cuffs click on your wrists.

win.text: You vault a fence and lose them in the alleys.

lose.text: A tackle ends the chase. A cold cell, a long night.

choices.label: Offer a bribe (@50)
choices.text: The envelope vanishes. "Have a good evening."

text: Your phone buzzes. It's {parent}. "Have you eaten properly?"

choices.label: Talk for a while (30m)
choices.text: You end up laughing about nothing. It helps more than you expected.

choices.label: Let it ring
choices.text: You tell yourself you'll call back later.

text: {sibling} messages you: "Can you help me out with @20 this week? I'll pay you back."

choices.label: Send @20
choices.text: {sibling} replies with a photo of a very bad meal. You laugh.

choices.label: Say you can't
choices.text: The silence afterward is awkward.

text: {spouse} is waiting up. "Sit with me a bit?"

choices.label: Sit together (1h)
choices.text: You talk about everything and nothing.

choices.label: Say you're too tired
choices.text: {spouse} nods, but you notice the look.

text: {child} comes to you with a problem that feels enormous to them.

choices.label: Listen properly (45m)
choices.text: Their whole face unclenches. You feel like a decent parent.

choices.label: Promise to talk later
choices.text: They nod. They've heard that before.

text: The apartment feels very quiet. Your thumb hovers over {friend}'s name.

choices.label: Send a message
choices.text: The reply is instant. You talk until your face hurts from smiling.

choices.label: Put the phone down
choices.text: You tell yourself they're probably busy.

text: Your chest is tight and everything feels like too much at once.

choices.label: Stop and breathe slowly
choices.text: In for four, out for six. The edges soften.

choices.label: Call {friend}
choices.text: You don't explain much. {friend} just stays on the line.

choices.label: Push through it
choices.text: You clench your jaw and keep going. It costs you.

text: The light catches the buildings just right and for a moment everything looks kind.

choices.label: Stop and take it in
choices.text: You stand there a while. Nobody minds.

choices.label: Keep walking
choices.text: You carry the feeling with you for a few streets.

text: A flyer on the library noticeboard: a small local scholarship, open to anyone who can write a good essay.

win.text: Weeks later a letter arrives. You won. +#80

lose.text: No reply ever comes, but the writing taught you something.

choices.label: Walk past
choices.text: You have enough on your plate.

text: A retired teacher at the next table notices you struggling. "Want a hand with that?"

choices.label: Accept the help (@5)
choices.text: An hour with someone who explains things properly is worth more than three alone.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.text: You wave them off and go back to your book.

text: You spot a folded banknote caught under a bench.

choices.label: Pocket it
choices.text: Small luck, but you'll take it.

text: Someone you barely know mentions their cousin is hiring, and that you seem like the type they'd want.

choices.label: Ask for an introduction
choices.text: A word in the right ear. Nothing life-changing, but it pays, and doors open a crack.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.text: You smile and change the subject.

text: A cyclist clips you at the crossing and keeps going. Your elbow throbs.

choices.label: Walk it off
choices.text: Wrong place, wrong second.

text: A pipe bursts in the wall above your bed. The landlord shrugs.

choices.label: Pay for the repair (@30)
choices.text: The bill is the kind that arrives with a sigh.

choices.label: Mop up and live with it
choices.text: The wall will smell for weeks.
